items.question: the AUTHORITATIVE confirmation: Abhinavabhāratī on śānta
items.verdict: **THE EXACT REASONING, IN ABHINAVA'S OWN WORDS: śānta's sthāyin = *tattvajñāna-janita-nirveda-prayaḥ* (the world-weariness born of the knowledge of truth); "śānta and bibhatsa occur in connection with mokṣa" (ABh XVIII.110); śānta↔mokṣa as vīra↔dharma, raudra↔artha, śṛṅgāra↔kāma. Recognition = tattvajñāna → nirveda (the pivot) → śānta. Peace is the underlying rasa because it is the felt of mokṣa, the goal the worldly goals serve**

items.question: Branch AY: is the difference real even at the Śiva level?
items.verdict: **THE COMPLETED REALISM: "manifestation is only logically possible due to the difference between Śiva and His power that is created" (TĀ 1/73-74) — the difference is real all the way up; "Śiva becomes everything at each instant" (TĀ 1/66) — NOT absolute monism. REFINEMENT: recognition does not collapse the many into a blank one; it recognizes the difference as Śiva's own free becoming (unity-in-difference)**

items.question: Branch X: is the direction felt?
items.verdict: **the felt is primary (camatkāra = "the primary characteristic of consciousness"); the inward-turn is felt as "the dense wonder of the supreme bliss" — the Solms↔rasa bridge, derived from the text**

items.question: is everything rooted in love? then what is FEAR?
items.verdict: **FEAR IS NOT THE OPPOSITE OF LOVE — it is love in the mode of threatened loss (the recoil). Grief = love lost, fear = love threatened, fury = love obstructed, disgust = love violated. The rope-snake: "the rope mistaken for a serpent does produce fear" — fear is real because the love it protects is real. Recognition releases the recoil; "where there is no fear at all" = the love at rest, having seen nothing it loves can be lost**

items.question: the HONEST crux (correcting the last session): how can the four painful emotions be pleasurable?
items.verdict: **THE CORRECTION: the "touch of bitterness" was too weak. The REAL resolution is the VIBHĀVA move: "when these causes are depicted in kāvya, they lose their character as causes and turn into vibhāvas... alaukika... as with love bites in sexual union, they produce pleasure and pleasure alone." The pleasure is RELOCATED to the alaukika tasting, not in the emotion. "Anger = love defended" is true of the EMOTION (painful); raudra is the delight tasting it (pleasurable). And the aesthetic resolution does NOT heal real grief — that is a separate move**

items.question: Branch Y: what is grace?
items.verdict: **grace (śaktipāta) is NOT external ("no transfer," no saṁkrāma) — it is the self-apprehension's own inward-return (svātantrya); grace = recognition, grace's felt = wonder**

items.question: THE HARDEST OBJECTIONS: anthropomorphism, "what is play?", "why would Śiva play when people suffer?", "is recognition a cop-out?"
items.verdict: **THE HONEST AUDIT: (1) anthropomorphism — "the 'I' denotes only pure consciousness (bodhamātra), not a person" (answered, but the human words may only be moved back); (2) "play" = a real category, defined negatively (free, non-instrumental, needless), but explains FORM not CONTENT; (3) the "want" is dissolved (no chooser), but the felt injustice remains and is not justified; (4) recognition is NOT a cop-out — suffering and wonder are real at DIFFERENT LEVELS (contracted self vs. ground), neither cancels the other — but its TRUTH and ADEQUACY are asserted, not proven; they live or die by whether one can live them**

items.question: what are the three impurities?
items.verdict: impurities = the powers *contracted* (āṇava=will as deficiency, māyīya=knowledge as duality, karma=action as binding)

items.question: parallels/counters: the IPVV kāryakāraṇatāvimarśa (V3-I) vs. the Tantrāloka
items.verdict: **PARALLELS: action = the will ("the will itself pervaded by its own heat has assumed three aspects"); "the will and its object are inherently one"; the difference is REAL — "the reflections are real, a true reflection, not a mistake" (pratibimbavāda). COUNTER RESOLVED: real difference = the self's reflection; impurity = the misreading as external separation. REFINEMENT: recognition removes the misreading, not the world — the world seen as "my own face"**

items.question: the five kañcukas + the self-emptying: why THIS way, why at all, why doesn't it change?
items.verdict: **THE ANSWER: the five (kalā/vidyā/rāga/kāla/niyati) are NOT arbitrary — they are the COMPLETE set of the dimensions of finite agency (why this way, answered); "why empty at all" has NO answer (a reason would make it unfree — the "Inexplicable"/anākhya); the contraction is fixed in FORM but free in CONTENT (why it doesn't change); "free will to empty" is the honest refusal of theodicy, not (only) a cop-out**

items.question: karma and rebirth: the mechanism, the theodicy, and the karma-vs-freedom crux
items.verdict: **THE MECHANISM: karma = the third impurity (āṇava → craving → māyā → vāsanā → rebirth), the instrumental cause of bhoga, governed by niyati (the law of karma). THE THEODICY: karma is not punishment but the play's contracted becoming unfolding lawfully. THE CRUX RESOLVED: freedom (svātantrya) at the one's level, law (niyati) at the contracted level — karma = freedom contracted into a lawful sequence (like time = non-temporal into succession)**

items.question: Branch CA: are karma and time the same contraction? + "empties itself out of free will"
items.verdict: **THE GEM: time (kāla) = the FORM of the contraction; karma (niyati) = its CONTENT — the same contraction. AND THE ROOT: "the one eternal consciousness... out of its own free will, empties itself to become the contracted individual consciousness" (TĀ 12210) — the contraction is an act of FREEDOM. Karma = the self-given law of the freedom's self-emptying; karma = freedom's own depth, not punishment; recognition = the free return**

items.question: Branch K: is time a real addition?
items.verdict: **time = the self-shaping of the non-temporal activity into succession (the tetralemma); the Present = the point of power (centuries before Connes–Rovelli)**

items.question: the GEM: love is the root — anger/fear/grief are love transformed (a geometry of vectors)
items.verdict: **THE CRUX-RESOLUTION: the four painful emotions are "pierced through by an element of joy" — "the essence of compact light... is transcendental delight... all the rasas consist essentially in transcendental delight... the painful ones are affected by a certain touch of bitterness." LOVE IS THE ORIGIN; grief=love-lost, fear=love-threatened, ANGER=LOVE-DEFENDED/BETRAYED/HURT, disgust=love-violated. Recognition = the return from the bitter coloring to the love that is its substrate**

items.question: the deepest synthesis: if nothing is added/removed, what differs?
items.verdict: **THE MASTER-KEY: bondage/liberation = the DIRECTION of the one continuous self-apprehension — outward into the object (ego, krama) vs. inward into itself (pure aham, akrama). Nothing added, only re-directed**

items.question: Branch BB: the crux — where does the real Śiva↔power difference become the māyā impurity?
items.verdict: **THE CRUX RESOLVED: the real difference is WITHIN the self (Śiva↔power, being↔becoming); māyā is the SAME difference projected as EXTERNAL ("forges the duality between one's own conscious nature and the flux of phenomena"), forged by the CRAVING born of the felt incompleteness ("in the craving to make full that which is not, the impurity called Māyā arises"). Recognition reverses the craving's projection, not the difference — the whole path reduces to ceasing the craving**

items.question: Branch BK: a mother losing her child IS suffering — is Abhinava really saying it's just a rasa?
items.verdict: **THE HONEST ANSWER: the text holds BOTH — the grief is REAL ("God destroys the suffering of His devotees"; "the liberated soul's only purpose is to grace others") AND the wonder is always there at the ground (constant presence + freedom). They are TWO LEVELS of one event; neither cancels the other. Recognition = the seeing of the ground, NOT the denial of the tears — the most compassionate claim, not the coldest**

items.question: FIRST-PERSON: I am the mother, my child is gone. If I recognize myself as Śiva, how does the suffering change, and why?
items.verdict: **THE CHANGE: recognition does NOT erase the grief — it re-positions it. (1) identity: "I am this grief" → "this grief is a flavor within the wonder that I am"; (2) rest: the grasping ceases, grief moves from pain (lack of rest) to restful tasting; (3) nature: the grief reveals itself as the LOVE tasted in its absence. WHY: suffering = rasa + identification; recognition removes the identification, not the rasa. The mother's tears become the karuṇa-rasa of the one — the love kept, tasted in the loss**

items.question: Branch D: the perceiver / universality
items.verdict: **the perceiver cannot be objectified (regress); the Self "shines forth but once" — universality = the continuity of the one Light across all modes (identity of subjectivity, not world-content)**

items.question: the practical question: what does one actually DO? (rasa vs recognition vs samādhi)
items.verdict: **THE PRACTICAL ANSWER: a ladder — (1) reduce the drive ("the vast majority have a great deal to do to reduce ignorance, Māyā and Karma"); (2) polish the mirror with rasa ("constant relishing... the mirror of the heart polished through constant repetition and study of poetry"); (3) carry the move into life (recognize the object as the self); (4) let go ("for the ready, simply letting go, doing nothing"). Rasa = training the felt register of recognition in the safe container; enjoyment is the rehearsal, recognition is the aim**

items.question: why must it be reflexive?
items.verdict: determination IS vimarśa (transcendental reflexivity); universality gap

items.question: why three powers/means?
items.verdict: powers = modes of vimarśa by degree of krama; will=akrama, knowledge=subtle-krama, action=gross-krama; liberation = reversal

items.question: the hardest question: how is rasa FELT (sva-saṁvedana) yet ALAUKIKA (beyond time/space)?
items.verdict: **THE GEM: rasa is felt-yet-alaukika because it is self-luminous (sva-saṁvedana, "because rasa is felt, therefore it exists") = the felt of the INWARD self-apprehension, which is akrama (timeless); rasa escapes the three defects (attachment, weakness, absorption) as the optimal inward turn; recognition and rasa are the same event — art is recognition practiced in the safe container of the fiction**

items.question: the hard one: how does rasa work + why is śānta the underlying rasa?
items.verdict: **THE DERIVATION: rasa works because emotion = camatkāra (the act of appearance = the self-relishing of consciousness), universalized by sādhāraṇīkaraṇa; the rasas differ by content-relation to the bliss; śānta = the camatkāra WITHOUT a screen = the common ground of all rasas (the "camatkāramātra" the text equates with blissful deep sleep)**

items.question: Branch AR: why does rasa differ from the perfect yogin's samādhi?
items.verdict: **THE GEM: samādhi is "overpowered by the Self" (absorbed, devoid of beauty); rasa keeps the inward turn as a FELT relish — "the essence of the compact Light is transcendental delight"; recognition is closer to rasa than to samādhi; the jīvanmukta is not absorbed but relishing the world-as-self — aesthetics is training in recognition's felt register**

items.question: Branch AD: is śānta the felt of the inward direction?
items.verdict: **THE UNIFYING GEM: śānta = the felt of the self-apprehension turned inward; the eight rasas = the felt of its outward turnings; the rasa-system IS the felt of the valence, with śānta as ground-zero — unifies the Tantrāloka's rasa, the master-key (direction), and the Solms/valence thesis (V = −dF/dt)**

items.question: Branch O: the self as undisclosed object
items.verdict: **two ahams (ego vs. pure aham); recognition = the senses recognizing each object "to be nothing but itself"; the removal of the ego's exhaustiveness-claim, nothing added**

items.question: Branch BH: at the level of the one, is suffering literally a RASA?
items.verdict: **THE THEODICY COMPLETED: "the nature of suffering is, essentially, a particular kind of wonder (camatkriyā)"; "all rasas are essentially pleasurable... it is one's own consciousness that consists of uniform bliss that is enjoyed, the emotions only lend variety." SUFFERING = RASA + IDENTIFICATION; the one (dancer) tastes suffering as a rasa, we suffer only when identified with the content — recognition = the return of the spectator to the dancer**

items.question: Branch AH: is suffering obstructed śānta?
items.verdict: **THE HEALING OF SUFFERING: suffering = the outward-turned camatkāra denied its rest ("a particular kind of wonder brought about by the absence of all hope," TĀ 25586); sādhāraṇīkaraṇa resets the valence by disengaging the drive (generalizing the object); recognition resets it permanently (the object recognized as the self) — recognition is the permanent valence-reset of suffering, and śānta is its resolution**

items.question: THE THEODICY: why does impurity arise? can things be impure? why would Śiva choose suffering?
items.verdict: **THE QUESTION IS DISSOLVED, NOT ANSWERED: duality = "the play occasioned by the fullness of one's own inherent bliss"; "Śaiva nondualism embraces both duality and nonduality" — nothing is REALLY impure (impurity = the misreading of the play as external); there is no chooser who picks suffering (fullness overflows into every state); liberation = "the perception of the dynamic unity of consciousness in each of its self-obscurations"**

items.question: Branch J: the upāyas as reversal
items.verdict: **liberation = progressive disclosure/unsealing of the already-present, by apoha (exclusion) — the epistemic mechanism of recognition-not-attainment**
